filesystem._comment: Official MCP filesystem server, scoped to the KB repo. Requires Node.js on PATH. Gives read_file/list_directory/etc, but search_files here only matches FILE NAMES, not content -- see kb_search. IF THIS TIMES OUT: npx is resolving the package over the network on every start. Fix it permanently with `npm i -g @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem`, after which --prefer-offline resolves from the local cache in milliseconds. Losing this server means the agent cannot read any file, so it is worth fixing rather than ignoring.

kb_search._comment: Custom in-repo MCP server (kb_search_server.py). Adds full-text content search + a fast ICM/doc index -- the official filesystem server can't search inside file contents.

kb_rag_search._comment: Custom in-repo MCP server (rag_search_server.py). Local vector-DB semantic search (meaning-based, not keyword-based) -- the tool for triage-style questions like 'what should I do when X is stuck'. Runs a background thread that re-syncs the index every KB_REINDEX_INTERVAL_SECONDS so edits made to the repo during the day stay searchable without a manual step.

my-icm-mcp-server-c03f0519._comment: Remote ICM MCP server. Same URL as your .vscode/mcp.json, which carries NO key -- meaning the server authenticates via the MCP OAuth flow, which is exactly why Copilot prompts you to sign in. "auth": "oauth" makes DuDu run that same flow: first connection opens a browser for consent, then the token is cached in backend/.oauth_tokens/ and refreshed silently. transport=streamable_http here rather than VS Code's type:http -- different client, same protocol.

quickcommerce._comment: Local wrapper (quickcommerce_server.py) around the QuickCommerce REST API. Same 7 tools as the hosted MCP -- search_products, get_item_details, check_delivery_eta, group_search, group_eta, check_credits, list_platforms -- but reliable with langchain-mcp-adapters (the hosted /mcp streamable-http endpoint fails the session handshake). Auth via QUICKCOMMERCE_API_KEY (X-API-Key). Skipped unless the key is set in .env.

serpapi._comment: Local wrapper (serpapi_server.py) around SerpAPI for real Google search: google_search (web), google_local (doctors/restaurants/places), google_shopping (products/prices). Auth via SERPAPI_API_KEY. Skipped unless the key is set in .env.

twilio._comment: Official Twilio MCP (@twilio-alpha/mcp) over stdio, narrowed to SMS ONLY. Twilio's MCP exposes ~197 tools by default, which is sent to the model on every request -- so it is filtered twice: --services/--tags limit what the SERVER generates (twilio_api_v2010 = the classic REST API, Api20100401Message = the Messages resource used to send SMS), and "only_tools" is a belt-and-braces allowlist on our side. Auth arg is ACCOUNT_SID/API_KEY:API_SECRET. Skipped unless all three are set in .env. Watch the startup log: it prints every tool the server offered, so you can tighten "only_tools" to the exact generated name.

swiggy_food._comment: Swiggy Builders Club -- official India MCP. OAuth 2.1 + PKCE with Dynamic Client Registration, which is exactly what mcp_oauth.py performs, so no client ID to apply for: the first connection registers this app and opens a browser for consent. Local/dev use needs no approval; production access requires applying at mcp.swiggy.com/builders/docs/operate/access with a demo video. Other servers: /im (Instamart, 13 tools) and /dineout (reservations, 8 tools) -- add them the same way once food works. Skipped unless ENABLE_SWIGGY=true.

zomato._comment: External remote MCP server for menu search / cart / QR checkout. URL and auth scheme should be confirmed against Zomato's own MCP docs before relying on this in production.
